message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need to know | |---------|-----------------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are earned by being the first to finish a round and by collecting the cards left in opponents’ hands. | | **Players** | 2–10 (standard deck). | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1–9, two “Skip”, two “Reverse”, two “Draw Two”) + 4 “Wild” + 4 “Wild Draw Four”. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card, apply its effect immediately (e.g., if it’s a “Draw Two”, the first player draws two cards and loses their turn). | | **Turn Order** | Players sit in a circle. The first player is the one to the left of the dealer. Turn order moves clockwise unless a “Reverse” card changes it. | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play **one** card that matches either the color or the number/symbol of the top card on the discard pile. If you have a Wild card, you can play it at any time and choose the new color. | | **Special Cards** | 1. **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
2. **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
3. **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
4. **Wild** – You choose the new color.
5. **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise you risk a challenge.) | | **Drawing** | If you cannot play a card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise your turn ends. | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have **exactly one card left**, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards their last card. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards still held by the other players: numbers = face value, Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Winning the Game** | The first player to reach the target score (commonly 500) wins. If you’re playing a shorter game, you can set a lower target or play a single round. | | **House Variations** | • **Draw‑Four Challenge** – If you suspect a player illegally used a Wild Draw Four, they can challenge. If the challenger is wrong, they draw 4 cards; if right, the challenger draws 6.
• **Stacking** – Some groups allow stacking of Draw Two or Draw Four cards (e.g., if you play a Draw Two, the next player can play another Draw Two to pass the penalty).
• **No “Draw Four” on the first turn** – Some rules forbid playing a Wild Draw Four as the very first card. | --- ### Quick Play‑through Example 1. **Deal**: Each player gets 7 cards. 2. **Start**: Flip top card – say it’s a Red 7. 3. **Player A** (first to play) has a Red 9 → plays it. 4. **Player B** has a Yellow 9 → plays it. 5. **Player C** has a “Draw Two” → plays it. Player D draws two cards and skips. 6. **Player E** has a “Wild” → plays it, chooses Green. 7. **Player F** has a Green 3 → plays it. 8. … and so on until someone discards their last card. --- ### Tips for New Players - **Keep track of colors** – If you’re low on a particular color, try to play a Wild to change the color to something you have more of. - **Watch the discard pile** – Knowing what cards have been played helps you anticipate opponents’ moves. - **Use “Skip” and “Reverse” strategically** – They can protect you from a “Draw Two” or “Wild Draw Four” if you’re about to be targeted. - **Remember “UNO”** – It’s a simple rule but can cost you 2 cards if you forget. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
